statement: You are given two strings of lowercase letters, text and pattern. Find every position where pattern occurs in text.

The Rabin–Karp method computes a rolling hash of pattern and of each window of text with the same length. Sliding the window one step updates its hash in constant time: remove the leftmost character's contribution and add the new rightmost character. Only when a window's hash equals the pattern's hash are the characters compared, which rules out false matches from hash collisions.
Return the list of every starting index i (0-based) such that text[i … i + pattern.length − 1] equals pattern, in increasing order. Occurrences may overlap. Return an empty list if there are none.

examples.explanation: "abra" begins the text at index 0 and appears again at index 7, at the end.
Every window of length 2 is "aa", so the pattern matches at all four start positions 0 to 3, each overlapping the next.
